# Superbrain

> A free, local-first markdown notes app that runs entirely in a browser tab. Point it at markdown you already have, or start a new vault, and get editing, backlinks, tags, comments and a graph view on top of ordinary .md files. There is no account, no server and no upload: notes live either in the browser's own storage or as real .md files in a folder on your computer. It installs as a PWA and works with no network.

Made by [Shrinath Prabhu](https://shrinath.me), from the makers of [OwlEye Analytics](https://owleye.dev).

## What it does

- **Bring your own markdown.** Import a folder, a .zip, or individual files. The folder structure is kept exactly as it was.
- **Links resolve both ways.** Wiki-style `[[links]]` and relative markdown links both work, and every note shows what links back to it.
- **A graph view.** See how notes connect, without the complexity of a full knowledge-graph tool.
- **Editing that stays plain.** A rich text editor over markdown that round-trips to plain .md, including tables and task lists.
- **Tags, comments and a TL;DR.** The summary is computed on the device with TextRank, not by calling a model.
- **Your choice of storage.** Browser storage, or a folder on disk where notes are ordinary files you can back up and open in any other editor. Switchable per vault at any time.
- **Optional password locking.** A browser-storage vault can be encrypted with AES-GCM when you close it. There is no recovery path by design.
- **Export.** One note as self-contained HTML, or a whole vault as a .zip.
- **Offline.** Installable, and fully usable with no network.

## Answers to common questions

- **Does anything leave my machine?** No. There is no backend. Notes are never uploaded.
- **Do I need an account?** No sign-up, no email, no login.
- **What files does it accept?** `.md` notes, and `.webp`, `.jpg`, `.avif`, `.gif`, `.png`, `.svg` images and `.mp4` video. A folder is only imported if it has at least one markdown file somewhere inside it.
- **Which browsers?** Any modern browser. Saving into a folder on your computer uses the File System Access API, so that part needs Chrome, Edge or Opera. Browser storage works everywhere.
- **Is it free?** Yes, and the source is public.
- **What is a "vault"?** One notebook: its own notes, folders, ordering and storage choice. You can have as many as you like, and each is separate.
